observations: The seam fixture compares the SAME world-space edge limits; it does not falsely compare adjacent pixels at different locations.
Native one-texel diagnostic gates are independently strengthened to byte-exact controls and staged blends by audit_spatial.py.
The existing shader two endpoints are reused only in controlled diagnostic vertices to demonstrate equal-weight sample-color blending; real upload integration and temporal semantics are not claimed.
SharedFlowReference.java uses bounded 17-entry distributions over four global corners; the support is at most nine neighboring cells. This executable reference is staged outside production.
The reference diagnostic is an analytic periodic function. Its still-water component is not validation of the real still sprite, tint, chemistry or alpha semantics.
Resource allocation here belongs to validation; production CPU/GPU vertex strides, bounded histories, shader texture cost and layout remain unchanged.
Stale/repeated upload, bounded-history and phase controls pass unchanged; no new cap churn, runtime profiling, real stream, page-boundary upload, mixed transparency or owner GPU acceptance follows.
Failed/rejected candidate is retained in validation and never merged into production or main.
review_limits: Shared corner weights/history/phase data must be carried through actual uploads with explicit resource budgets before promoting a fix.
A naive full distribution requires up to nine unique texture evaluations per fragment; a bounded practical implementation and matched profiling are still required.
Independent source extraction and controlled shader evidence do not close full engine acceptance.
